old_title: Breaking: WA government to appeal $150m Andrew Forrest Fortescue native title payout
new_title: WA government to appeal $150m Andrew Forrest Fortescue native title payout
old_text:
Mining magnate Andrew Forrest's Fortescue faces a renewed legal battle over a record $150.3 million native title compensation payout, with the WA government confirming it would appeal a landmark Federal Court judgement.
It comes after the Yindjibarndi native title group announced they would also appeal the amount awarded, renewing a bitter dispute with Mr Forrest's company.
The Federal Court had found Fortescue liable for $150 million in cultural losses, and $150,000 in economic losses, plus interest.
At the core of the dispute was the construction of four Pilbara iron ore mines without permission from the Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation.
In a statement confirming its appeal, Attorney General Tony Buti said the state government supported "proper compensation" for the impact of mining on country.
"As this is a matter which is currently before the court, it would not be appropriate to comment on the specifics of the case at this time."
It's unclear what grounds the WA government is appealing the judgement on.
Legal battle
The $150 million judgement was the culmination of an almost two-decades long legal battle between the Yindjibarndi people and Fortescue.
Some Elders had expressed disappointment at the amount awarded when compared to the billions the mining company had made from its lucrative Solomon Hub mines, built on Yindjibarndi land.
Traditional Owners and Fortescue had attempted to negotiate land use agreements in the past, but never reached a consensus.
In a statement, Yindjibarndi Group CEO Michael Woodley said the Aboriginal corporation's decision to appeal came after a unanimous vote.
He said both Fortescue and the WA government had argued in court for lower compensation amounts.
"The state government has a responsibility to also provide support and protection to the Yindjibarndi community from miners," Mr Woodley had said.

WA government to appeal landmark native title ruling against Andrew Forrest's Fortescue
In short:
The WA government is appealing the decision by a Federal Court to award the Yindjibarndi native title group a record $150.3 million in compensation for the construction of iron ore mines on their land without permission.
The decision to appeal comes after the indigenous group announced they would also appeal the amount, which billionaire Andrew Forrest's company Fortescue is liable to pay.
The Yindjibarndi Ngurra Aboriginal Corporation says it is disappointed with the compensation while both the WA government and Fortescue had argued in court for a lower amount.
